To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) The use of the TCP/IP protocol family has been successful in HEP, and (ii) The use of OSI protocols is not yet mature enough to be recommended for use in HEP.
we have found a way to connect a few thousand computers to the Internet, that the Internet is a reliable, fast and flexible network and that it is a good idea to use standard software.
we have found that the OSI model is a good model for HEP networking and that it can be implemented using the products of a number of vendors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a distributed computing environment for the LEP experiments and the LHC experiments, and the development and operation of the LHC computing grid.

the following aspects: - The development of a distributed file system for HEP, based on a distributed file server, a distributed file cache, a distributed file name server, a distributed access protocol and a file system interface; - The development of an integrated HEP communication system based on the ISO OSI Reference Model, with the aim to provide a uniform and integrated access to a wide variety of communication services, such as remote file access, electronic mail, remote job submission, remote terminal access, etc; -
two major areas: 1) the development of the network infrastructure for the CERN community, 2) the development of applications which will use these facilities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CERN is now in a position to provide a wide range of networking services to its users, and that these services are used by an ever-increasing number of users.
we now have a network infrastructure which will support the needs of HEP for the next 3-5 years, and which will continue to evolve in response to new developments in HEP.
we are now able to provide a networked HEP environment which can be relied upon to be available, stable, efficient, and flexible enough to meet the needs of HEP.

the first generation of products is being installed and used.
we have moved from the experimental phase into the operational and production phase.

, while the last two years have not been marked by spectacular developments in networking, they have been years of real progress and of a lot of work, and that this work has been rewarded with the use of real, working networks.

the use of real, industrial, networks is a reality and that the future is not only bright but already here.
